name: Kunal Garg

papers.title: BarrierFormer: Transformer-Guided Predictive Barrier Enforcement for Safe Robot Control
papers.abstract: Control barrier functions (CBFs) have become one of the most popular tools for encoding and enforcing state constraints in safety-critical robotics. Standard CBF approaches are inherently myopic in nature as they enforce safety only at the current time step. Consequently, the system can be driven toward the boundary of the safe set where no feasible safe control exists at a future timestep. Model predictive control (MPC) based approaches address this by enforcing state constraints over a receding horizon. However, such approaches require solving a constrained optimization problem at every step, which is computationally expensive for real-time deployment. We propose BarrierFormer, a barrier-supervised transformer framework that addresses these limitations by encoding rollout-level CBF constraints in learning a safe policy. A causal transformer encodes observation-action history, outputs a residual correction to a nominal controller through the action head, and autoregressively generates a predictive rollout through the dynamics head. A barrier critic operating on local observations evaluates CBF constraint violations along this rollout, and a safety teacher computes barrier-consistent actions satisfying these constraints as direct supervision targets for the control policy. During inference, the policy maps observation-action history to control actions without any online optimization, enabling real-time usage of the proposed history-based predictive safety enforcement. Evaluations across linear and nonlinear dynamical systems for safe goal-directed navigation show that BarrierFormer outperforms reinforcement learning (RL)-based, diffusion-based, MPC-based, and transformer-based baselines in safety rate, success rate, and inference latency.
